T>\nT kahan_sum(const std::vector<T>& data) {\n    T sum = 0.0;\n    T c = 0.0;\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        T y = val - c;\n        T t = sum + y;\n        c = (t - sum) - y;\n for (int i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {\n        printf(\"Sample[%zu]: %.17e\\n\", indices[i], static_cast<double>(data[indices[i]]));\n    }\n    printf(\"Hash: %016\" PRIx64 \"\\n\", h.get());\n    printf(\"=== END RESULTS ===\\n\");\n}\n\n// Print results for integer arrays (uses exact hash comparison)\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid print_results_int(const std::vector<T>& data, const char* name = <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Simple Cholesky decomposition (sequential, unblocked algorithm)\n// Decomposes positive definite matrix A into L * L^T where L is lower triangular\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            \n            if (i == j) {\n                // Diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n                if (val <= 0.0) {\n                    // Matrix is not positive definite\n                    printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                    return false;\n                }\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            } else {\n                // Off-diagonal element\n                for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                    sum += A[i * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n                }\n                A[i * n + j] = (A[i * n + j] - sum) / A[j * n + j];\n            }\n        }\n        \n        // Zero out upper triangular part\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n    \n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n    \n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n    \n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n","userModified":false}}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfg9WstuqJBwWd2sFyVe7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I rewrote `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program and updated `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`. The executable is still `cholesky`, no new files were created, and the only libraries used are MPI, OpenMP and the CUDA runtime (no cuBLAS). Results validate on 1–4 ranks for every size I tried, from n=1 up to n=16384. The not-positive-definite case prints the same error message and diagonal index as the original and exits with code 1.\n\n**How it's split up**\n- **MPI:** the matrix is divided into block columns spread round-robin across ranks, one GPU per rank. At each step, the rank owning the current block column factors it and the result is shared with all ranks.\n  - Within a node, ranks share host memory, and each GPU copies the panel directly in and out of it. My first version used `MPI_Bcast`, which reached only about 2 GB/s here.\n  - Across nodes, one rank per node does the broadcast. I've only tested this on one node, so the multi-node path is untested.\n- **CUDA:** custom double-precision kernels for the matrix-multiply update, the triangular solve and the small diagonal-block factorization. The next block column is factored on a high-priority stream while the rest of the update runs on another, and copies overlap with computation.\n- **OpenMP:** matrix generation, assembling the result on rank 0 from the broadcast pieces (so there's no separate gather at the end), and validation.\n- **Block width** is picked from the matrix size and number of ranks: wider blocks are faster on one GPU, narrower ones scale better across several.\n\n**Correctness**\n- The generated input matrix is bit-identical to the original's.\n- Output sums match the original sequential code exactly for n = 100, 512, 1000, 2049 and 3000.\n- The blocked algorithm still changes rounding slightly. The largest relative error against the original matrix was 2.9e-9 at n=16384, well under the 1e-6 tolerance.\n\n**Performance** (RTX 3090s, best of repeated runs; the machine was heavily loaded by other users, so single runs vary noticeably)\n\n| n | 1 GPU | 4 GPUs |\n|---|---|---|\n| 8192 | 353 ms | 152 ms (~1.1 TFLOPS) |\n| 16384 | 2553 ms (~575 GFLOPS) | 735 ms (~2.0 TFLOPS) |\n| 24576 | 8171 ms | 2304 ms (~2.15 TFLOPS) |\n\nFor comparison, the original sequential code takes about 235 ms at n=1000; this version takes 5–7 ms with 4 ranks. One GPU runs at about 575–605 GFLOPS, close to the card's double-precision peak, and 4 GPUs are 3.5× faster than one at n=16384.\n\n**Things to know**\n- **Timer coverage:** the timer covers uploading each rank's data to its GPU, the factorization, and assembling the full result on rank 0. Matrix generation and GPU memory allocation happen before the timer starts.\n- **Thread count:** if `OMP_NUM_THREADS` isn't set, each rank uses its share of the node's cores.\n- **How to run:** `mpirun -np <number of GPUs> ./cholesky -n N [-v] [-r]`. When ranks aren't bound to cores, I used `--bind-to none`.\n- **Original source:** I overwrote `cholesky.cpp` without making a backup. The reference I compared against was rebuilt in /tmp from my earlier read-out of the file, so you'll need version control or another copy if you want the original back."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":487,"cache_read_input_tokens":118779,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":487},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"4b7a45ce-17a2-4c41-89da-1822177290f8","uuid":"2a75db11-d5ec-4fa8-9755-bcae486b6f0a","timestamp":"2026-10-03T23:10:28.345Z","request_id":"req_011Cfg9WryLVpACspkvsHhTY"}
